idiom_name: node struct with a hand-built function-pointer table (vtable) and a child pointer array
implementation_notes: C has neither classes nor virtual dispatch, so the Component/Leaf/Composite roles are built from structs: a base struct holding a pointer to a table of function pointers stands in for the abstract Component, derived structs embed that base as their first member (the standard single-inheritance trick), and a container keeps a heap-allocated array of Component* children plus a count and a capacity. The uniform operation is a dispatcher that follows the table pointer - shape_area(me) becomes me->ops->area(me) - and the container's implementation loops over its children calling the same dispatcher. A tagged struct with a switch over an enum node kind is the lighter alternative when the node set is fixed and never extended from outside. Keep the hand-built vtable when nodes must be polymorphic and extensible; for a single container shape, plain structs plus a recursive function are cheaper and safer.
pitfalls: Every downcast from the base struct to the container struct is unchecked: a wrong table or a reordered struct is undefined behaviour that the compiler cannot catch.
There is no destructor chain - the container must free its children recursively, so a missing free leaks a whole subtree and a child reachable from two parents is freed twice.
The base struct must remain the first member of every derived struct; moving it breaks every cast silently.
